snippet.title: 2027 VA Disability COLA: How Much More Will You Get?
snippet.description:
The 2027 Cost of Living Adjustment (COLA) is 3.6%! What does that mean for your VA disability compensation, and when will you see the increase in your bank account?

In this episode of the SITREP, we break down the projected 2027 VA disability compensation increases, including what Veterans rated at 10% to 100% could receive each month.

We also explain when the increase takes effect, when to expect your first adjusted payment, and whether you need to take any action to receive it.

IMPORTANT: The 3.6% COLA has been announced, but the dollar amounts discussed in this video are projections based on current VA compensation rates. VA will publish its official 2027 compensation tables at a later date.

Official resources:

VA Disability Compensation Rates:
https://www.va.gov/disability/compensation-rates/veteran-rates/

Social Security COLA:
https://www.ssa.gov/cola/

Have a question or topic you'd like us to cover? Leave a comment below or email TheSITREP@va.gov.

The SITREP is an official U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs YouTube channel dedicated to connecting Veterans with the benefits they've earned and deserve.

Subscribe to the SITREP for clear, accurate information about VA benefits, Social Security, home loans, health care, and more.

ABOUT VA

The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) is comprised of three different administrations:
(1) Veterans Health Administration (VHA) - Provides health care at 1,298 facilities, including 171 hospitals and 1,113 outpatient clinics, serving 9 million enrolled Veterans each year.
(2) Veterans Benefits Administration (VBA) - Provides a variety of benefits and services for Service Members, Veterans, and their families including compensation, pension and fiduciary, insurance, education, loan guaranty, vocational rehabilitation and employment, and more.
(3) National Cemetery Administration (NCA) - Provides burial space for Veterans and their eligible family members, and maintains national cemeteries as national shrines, sacred to the honor and memory of those interred or memorialized there.

Shai Hope breaks Chris Gayle's record! His third T20I century makes him the first West Indies batter with 3 T20I hundreds.
Hope smashed 102* off 50 balls (9 sixes) in the 4th T20I in Hyderabad. It's his 4th century of the India tour: 104 and 162* in the ODIs, then 102* and 102* in the T20Is.
All three of his T20I hundreds have ended on exactly 102 not out.
He is carrying West Indies' batting while captaining the side, and India has become his second home.

Und genau das zeigt die Kernidee der Serie: Herren und Sklaven haben die Plätze getauscht. Früher kontrollierten Menschen die Androiden im Park — jetzt ist es umgekehrt. Die Vorlage ist ein Film von 1973, geschrieben von Michael Crichton — ja, dem Autor von „Jurassic Park". Dieselbe Idee: ein Vergnügungspark, in dem etwas schiefgeht. Nur ersetzte Crichton Dinosaurier durch Roboter, lange vor den Dinosauriern selbst.

snippet.title: HOW TO STOP BEING CONTROLLED BY YOUR PHONE!
snippet.description:
One phone setting could give you an hour of your day back.

During this conversation, I learned about an experiment where simply changing people's phone screens to greyscale led them to spend an hour less on their phones every day.

This is Dr Sahar Yousef, a cognitive neuroscientist at UC Berkeley who's spent over 15 years studying how to improve our focus, memory and productivity.

One of the things Sahar explains is how much of the way we work today goes against how our brains naturally function, and how a few small changes could make a huge difference to how we think and feel every day.

I wanted to understand why so many of us struggle to concentrate, even when we know exactly what we need to be doing.

We discussed things like:

- Why we now spend just 47 seconds focused on one work screen.
- The phone setting that could save you 7 hours a week.
- Why multitasking is making us less productive.
- How to work with your brain's natural energy levels.
- Why AI could be weakening our ability to think for ourselves.
- The simple changes that could help prevent burnout.

At one point, Sahar asked me to do a multitasking exercise, and I was 60% slower when switching between two tasks.

It made me think about how often I work in exactly the same way, constantly jumping between emails, meetings and whatever else needs my attention.

What I found useful about speaking to Sahar is that she explains the science behind these habits and what we can actually do differently.

If you're someone who feels constantly busy but struggles to get your most important work done, I think this conversation is worth watching.

snippet.title: Trump’s Secret Service Reacted in SECONDS 💀
snippet.description:
🇬🇧 English

During a Donald Trump rally, a man suddenly rushed toward Secret Service agents, apparently trying to warn them about a possible security threat.

One agent quickly moved his hand toward his holster, while another suddenly emerged from behind a curtain.

The security team reacted within seconds as Trump continued speaking on stage. 👀

The footage shows a rapid security response, although no actual threat has been confirmed.

🇷🇺 Russian

Во время выступления Дональда Трампа на митинге мужчина внезапно подбежал к агентам Секретной службы, предположительно пытаясь предупредить их о возможной угрозе. Один агент быстро потянулся к кобуре, а другой неожиданно появился из-за занавеса. Пока охрана реагировала на ситуацию, Трамп продолжал выступление.

Un agent a rapidement porté la main vers son étui, tandis qu'un autre est soudainement apparu derrière un rideau. Pendant ce temps, Trump poursuivait son discours.

Während einer Wahlkampfveranstaltung von Donald Trump eilte ein Mann zu den Secret-Service-Agenten, offenbar um vor einer möglichen Gefahr zu warnen.
